text: What if you could use one hundred percent of your brain?
The story goes that we only use ten percent. That's a myth. But let's pretend the switch exists, and flip it at sunrise.
By mid-morning, you'd learn a new language before breakfast, and read an entire library before lunch.
At noon, perfect recall. Every face, every number, every moment of your life, instantly available.
But by sunset, there's a cost. Your brain already burns a fifth of your energy. At full power, you'd have to eat around the clock.
And at midnight, when every neuron fires at once, that isn't genius. That's a seizure.
The truth? You already use all of your brain. Just never all at once.
